title: TS: cancelSignal doesn't abort the in-flight Bedrock stream — generation and billing continue after cancel
body:
### Checks

- [x] I have updated to the lastest minor and patch version of Strands
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched [./issues](./issues?q=) and there are no duplicates of my issue

### SDK Language

TypeScript

### Strands Version

1.9.0 (root cause also verified on current `main`)

### Language Runtime Version

Node 20 / Node 22

### Operating System

Amazon Linux 2023 (AWS Lambda)

### Installation Method

npm

### Steps to Reproduce

```ts
const controller = new AbortController()
const run = (async () => {
  for await (const _ of agent.streamAsync('Write a 2000+ word essay.', { cancelSignal: controller.signal })) {}
})()
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000)
await run
```

Use a fast-streaming Bedrock model and watch CloudWatch Bedrock output-token metrics (or a proxy on the h2 stream) after the abort.

### Expected Behavior

Cancelling a turn aborts the in-flight model request, so the provider stops generating (and billing) promptly.

### Actual Behavior

The local `for await` loop stops quickly, but the Bedrock ConverseStream request is never aborted — the model keeps generating server-side and output tokens keep billing until the turn hits a natural message boundary. With a fast token stream we measured ~27s of continued generation/billing after cancel. With the signal threaded into the transport (see below), generation and billing stop within ~6ms–1.5s (CloudWatch-verified).

### Additional Context

The signal is only checked between stream events, never passed to the transport:

- `strands-ts/src/models/bedrock.ts` L629-630: `this._client.send(command)` — no send options, so no `abortSignal` reaches the AWS SDK request handler. Same for the non-streaming path at L644-645.
- `strands-ts/src/agent/agent.ts` L2154-2155: `_throwIfCancelled()` runs inside the `while (!result.done)` loop, i.e. between yielded events. Throwing `CancelledError` unwinds the local iteration but the HTTP/2 stream stays open.

Separate smaller thing (will file separately if wanted): on `CancelledError` the agent appends a synthetic `'Cancelled by user'` assistant message (`agent.ts` L1687), which pollutes history for apps that render their own cancel state. An opt-out would help.

### Possible Solution

Pass the signal through to `this._client.send(command, { abortSignal })`, and destroy the streaming response body when the signal fires — in practice the body destroy is what reliably ends the h2 stream mid-flight. Needs the signal plumbed from the agent loop through `Model.stream()` to the provider; the Agent already holds it (`agent.ts` L1072-1073).

We run this in production as a `BedrockModel` subclass and it works well — happy to open a PR if you're open to it.

### Related Issues

None found on this. Loosely adjacent: #3050, #1819.
